pahl.estimator: Theil-Sen slope of log excess attention over 90 days after the peak; PAHL = ln2/lambda
pahl.primary_excess_baseline: median log attention over [-90,-30] days before the event

spike_vs_pahl.interpretation: negative rho means larger announcement spikes have shorter PAHL (regression to the mean); interpret alongside the spike placebo

placebo.method: For each event, 500 random calendar dates in the same year (within data bounds) are treated as pseudo-ceasefires and PAHL is estimated with the identical pipeline; the study-level null draws one placebo PAHL per event and takes the median across events.

spike.method: Peak excess = max over [0, +14] days of the 7-day centred-median log attention minus the pre-event baseline ([-90,-30]), averaged across language editions. 500 random same-year dates per event are pushed through the identical statistic; the study-level null draws one placebo per event and takes the median across events.

prediction.primary_model: resumption ~ z(PAHL) (univariate; auc_in_sample/auc_cv refer to this model)
prediction.model_formula: primary (univariate): P(resumption=1) = logit^-1(a + b * z(PAHL)); adjusted: + c * log1p(pre-event 6-month mean monthly fatalities) + C(agreement_type) + C(region)
prediction.note: n is small and the models are exploratory; no causal interpretation. Cross-validated AUC is reported alongside in-sample AUC because the latter is optimistic.

adjusted_model.formula: resumption ~ z(PAHL) + log1p(pre fatalities) + C(agreement_type) + C(region)

survival.ci_scale: log hazard (coefficient scale); hr_ci_* are hazard-ratio CIs
survival.duration_definition: months from event month to first qualifying resumption run; censored at 12

crossing_method.method: smoothed excess crosses half its peak; horizon 180 days

leave_one_out.note: PAHL LOO: median recomputed with each event deleted. AUC LOO: leave-one-event-out predictive AUC plus the distribution of refitted in-sample AUCs on the remaining events.

permutation.statistic: standardised logistic coefficient of PAHL (ridge penalty)

baseline_sensitivity.note: decay fitted on excess over the 28-day centred rolling baseline (vs the fixed pre-event baseline used for the primary estimate)

event_study.peak_statistic: peak_mean_excess is the maximum of the 7-day centred median of the daily cross-event mean excess curve (the curve used to locate peak_day); peak_mean_excess_daily is the unsmoothed daily mean at that day, and day0_mean_excess is the unsmoothed daily mean at t=0
event_study.baseline: 28-day centred rolling mean with +/-14 day event mask (DESIGN.md)

checks.war_vs_peace_direction: peace_decays_slower (WAR basket median PAHL < PEACE basket median PAHL)

falsification.summary: Two placebo tests are reported. The SPIKE placebo asks whether the attention response itself is event-specific (claim A); the DECAY placebo asks whether the post-peak decay rate is event-specific (claim B). They answer different questions and must be read separately. A failed decay placebo means PAHL should not be interpreted as an event-specific decay rate even if the spike is event-specific. A non-significant permutation test means the PAHL-resumption association does not survive randomisation and no predictive claim is supported.
